questions.q_en:
Match the following organizations with their headquarters:

List IList II
i. Food and Agriculture Organizationa. New York
ii. World Bankb. Rome
iii. International Labour Organizationc. Washington D.C.
iv. United Nationsd. Geneva
questions.solution_en:
Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) - Rome, Italy

o The FAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security.

o Established in 1945, its headquarters are located in Rome, Italy, near the historic center of the city.

o The FAO works with member countries to promote sustainable agricultural practices, improve rural development, and ensure access to nutritious food for all.

o It also provides data and analysis on global food systems, fisheries, forestry, and climate change impacts on agriculture.

o The organization collaborates with governments, NGOs, and other UN agencies to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 2 (Zero Hunger).

World Bank - Washington D.C., USA

o The World Bank is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to governments of low- and middle-income countries for development projects.

o Founded in 1944, its headquarters are in Washington D.C., USA, near the White House and other major international institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

o The World Bank focuses on reducing poverty and supporting economic development through projects in areas such as education, health, infrastructure, and environmental sustainability.

o It consists of two main institutions: the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA).

o The World Bank also conducts research and provides policy advice to help countries address global challenges like climate change and inequality.

International Labour Organization (ILO) - Geneva, Switzerland

o The ILO is a UN agency dedicated to promoting social justice and internationally recognized labor rights.

o Established in 1919, it is the oldest specialized agency of the UN, with its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, near other international organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO).

o The ILO sets international labor standards, develops policies, and creates programs to promote decent work for all, including fair wages, safe working conditions, and social protection.

o It operates on a tripartite structure, bringing together governments, employers, and workers from its 187 member states.

o The ILO also addresses issues such as child labor, forced labor, and workplace discrimination.

United Nations Headquarters - New York, USA

o The United Nations Headquarters is the primary office of the UN, serving as the central hub for its global operations.

o Located in New York City, USA, the complex sits along the East River in Manhattan and is an iconic symbol of international diplomacy.

o The headquarters houses the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, and the Secretariat, among other key bodies.

o It serves as a forum for member states to discuss and address global issues such as peace and security, human rights, sustainable development, and international law.

o The UN Headquarters also hosts major international conferences and summits, bringing together world leaders, diplomats, and civil society representatives.

Only individuals can bring cases before the ICJ

questions.q_en:
Match the following Indian organizations with their establishment years:

List IList II
i. Central Bureau of Investigationa. 1964
ii. National Human Rights Commissionb. 1963
iii. National Green Tribunalc. 1993
iv. National Investigation Agencyd. 2010
questions.solution_en:
Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) - 1963

o The CBI is India's premier investigative agency, functioning under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances, and Pensions.

o It was established on April 1, 1963, by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs, based on the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption.

o The CBI is responsible for investigating serious crimes, including corruption, economic offenses, organized crime, and high-profile cases referred by the central government, state governments, or the judiciary.

o It also handles cases of national and international importance, such as terrorism, cybercrime, and human trafficking.

o The CBI is often referred to as the "Indian FBI" and operates under the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.

o Its headquarters is located in New Delhi, with regional offices across India.

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) - 1993

o The NHRC is an independent statutory body established on October 12, 1993, under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993.

o It was created to protect and promote human rights in India, as defined by the Indian Constitution and international covenants.

o The NHRC investigates complaints of human rights violations by public authorities, including police and security forces, and recommends corrective measures.

o It also conducts research, spreads awareness about human rights, and advises the government on policy matters related to human rights.

o The commission consists of a chairperson (usually a retired Chief Justice of India) and other members with expertise in human rights, law, and social issues.

o Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

National Green Tribunal (NGT) - 2010

o The NGT was established on October 18, 2010, under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, to handle cases related to environmental protection and conservation.

o It was created to provide a specialized forum for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases involving environmental issues, such as pollution, forest conservation, and biodiversity.

o The NGT has the power to hear cases related to environmental laws, including the Water Act, Air Act, Forest Conservation Act, and Environmental Protection Act.

o It operates on the principle of sustainable development and follows a "polluter pays" approach.

o The tribunal has its principal bench in New Delhi and regional benches in cities like Pune, Bhopal, Chennai, and Kolkata.

National Investigation Agency (NIA) - 2008

o The NIA was established on December 31, 2008, following the passage of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008, in the wake of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks.

o It became operational in 2009 and is India's central counter-terrorism agency.

o The NIA is tasked with investigating and prosecuting offenses affecting the sovereignty, security, and integrity of India, including terrorism, insurgency, and transnational crimes.

o It has jurisdiction over cases across India and can take up cases referred by state governments or the central government.

o The agency is headquartered in New Delhi and has regional offices in various parts of the country.

o The NIA works closely with state police forces, intelligence agencies, and international organizations to combat terrorism and organized crime.
